critique: The charcoal, oxidized gray, rust, brass, and cyan palette is disciplined, and the square tile grammar gives the board a sturdy industrial identity. The board still shows construction inconsistencies: floor tiles have inset gradients while wall tiles use diagonal stripes, yet both share uneven dark seams; object outlines and shadows vary widely between crates, player, goals, lever, and door. The lever is rendered with smooth rounded geometry while goals are highly detailed radial symbols and the player is a glossy ring, so interactables do not feel cut from one asset set. Very small low-contrast instructional copy and status lines reduce typographic finish, and the board's large black unused strip on the right reads as an untrimmed container.
suggestion: Trim the board container precisely to the 10-column grid and establish one tile-gap, border, and inset-shadow token. Redraw every interactable on a shared icon grid with consistent outline weight, highlight direction, shadow depth, and limited material rules—wood for crates/door, brass for targets/lever, cyan for player. Standardize sidebar card borders, heading tracking, body size, and status colors, increasing small-text contrast. Align both side modules and header HUD to the board's grid lines and remove residual empty container space so the screen feels intentionally fabricated rather than debug-layout adjacent.
audit_note: Direct independent visual critique from the r0 screenshot and brief only; no generation notes, HTML, other critics, revisions, or scores were inspected.
